newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PAL files suit vs official on Singapore air accord.
newsitem.headline: PAL files suit vs official on Singapore air accord.

text.p: Philippine Airlines (PAL) said on Friday it had filed suit against a government official, saying he favoured Singapore carriers by amending an air agreement.
PAL said it had lost $4.5 million in revenues since 1996 after Civil Aeronautics Board director Victor Limlingan increased the passenger capacity of Singapore carriers flying to the Philippines.

Limlingan had unilaterally amended an air agreement that was "unfairly favourable to Singapore carriers and damaging to the Philippine national carrier", PAL president Jose Antonio Garcia said in a statement.
"As a result of Limlingan's unilateral action, PAL suffered actual damages amounting to $4.5 million in the form of lost revenues," the statement said.
PAL is making losses due to higher operating expenses and lease charges. It posted a 1.41 billion peso loss in its fourth quarter which ended March 31 this year.
PAL said Limlingan allowed Singapore carriers to fly more frequently to the Philippines to the detriment of PAL flights.
"I'm surprised on what they did," Limlingan told Reuters when asked for comment, saying his action was proper and was upheld by the Civil Aeronautics Board last week.
He said the decision to allow higher flight frequencies rested on the negotiating panel that he headed. The panel was given full authority by the transportation secretary to revise any air agreement.
PAL said Limlingan did not consult nor seek the approval of the CAB as well as confirmation from the Office of the President. Limlingan said prior approvals were not necessary.
The petition to increase the capacity was initiated by a local cargo airline that said it needed to expand its capacity to Singapore due to higher bilateral trade.
In return, the Philippines allowed Singapore's Silk Air to fly more frequently to the central Cebu city and southern Davao city.
Limlingan is presently negotiating for another increase in flight frequencies between Singapore and the Philippines, as two new Philippine carriers were seeking access to Singapore.
